newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: BOTSWANA STOCKS WEEK - DOMESTIC INDEX RISES 3.2 PCT.
newsitem.headline: BOTSWANA STOCKS WEEK - DOMESTIC INDEX RISES 3.2 PCT.

text.p: The domestic index posted its
fifth highest weekly gain on the Botswana Stock Exchange in the
week ending April 11, rising 12.9 points, or 3.2 percent, to
Brewery holding company Sechaba Investment Co rose
20 thebe to 300. Banks all showed gains including Barclays
which increased 50 thebe to reach 690, First National
Bank rose five thebe to 490, Standard Chartered Bank
Botswana , which was not traded, was bid up 10 thebe to
Trading unchanged were Botswana Insurance at 220
thebe, investment company Kgola ya Sechaba at 18O thebe
and clothing chain Pep at 280 thebe.
Oil company Engen was bid at 445 thebe and offered
at 475, but did not trade. Also untraded were security group
Inco which was bid at 80 thebe and offered 85, food
and tobacco wholesaler Metsef bid at 645 thebe.
Variable loan stock company RDC Properties was bid
at 160 thebe and offered at 170 thebe, but did not trade, as did
food wholesaler Sefalana which was bid at 435 thebe
and offered at 440 thebe.
Domestic turnover declined with 23,600 shares compared to
1,082,400 the previous week, changing hands for a total value of
61,510 pula compared to an earlier 2,979,445 pula.
On the foreign board, De Beers rose 120 thebe to
trade at 13,138 and McCarthy Retail group ended its
first week on the BSE at 1,142 thebe. Undervalued Asset Fund
Regent was untraded.
The foreign index rose 3.56 points to 407.27. Turnover in
dual listed shares increased with 900 shares traded compared to
a previous 300.
The All Companies Index finished the week at 407.61 points
against 403.81.
